agency: Department of Public Works — Division of Water & Sewer
project_title: Sod Run WWTP Ultraviolet Disinfection Conversion Project
verbatim_excerpt: Harford County Capital Improvement Program (FY 2025-2026): Sod Run Ultraviolet Disinfection Project allocated $9,000,000 in Water & Sewer Enterprise capital funds to replace aging chlorine contact disinfection infrastructure past useful life with high-efficiency open-channel UV disinfection banks, PLC master control cabinets, automatic sleeve-wiping actuators, and online UV transmittance (UVT) sensors to meet stringent Chesapeake Bay NPDES effluent mandates.

agency: Public Works Department — Water & Sewer Utilities
project_title: Water & Sanitary Lift Station SCADA Telemetry Upgrades
verbatim_excerpt: City of Warrenville FY 2026 Adopted Budget & Council Agenda (Resolution R2025-39 context): Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) Improvements for municipal lift stations and wellfield water system budgeted at $300,000 in FY 2026 ($125,000 Water Utility Fund and $175,000 Sewer Utility Fund, plus $37,388 scheduled carryover) to replace obsolete radio telemetry, NEMA 4X RTU control panels, and cellular failover modems past useful life.

project_title: Southeast SCADA Tower & Telemetry Network Replacement (District 5)
verbatim_excerpt: Manatee County Adopted Capital Improvement Plan (Project #PJTP27015, District 5): Southeast SCADA Tower Replacement programmed at $2,157,000 via Water and Wastewater Utility Rate Funds. Scope includes dedicated wastewater SCADA communications tower replacement, licensed microwave/spread-spectrum radio transceivers, uninterruptible power supplies, and remote lift station RTU polling hardware for hurricane resiliency and SSO prevention.

agency: Manatee County Utilities Department — Wastewater Collection
spec_contact_role: Master Lift Station Capital Project Engineer
project_title: District 4 12A Master Lift Station Pump, MCC & SCADA Floodproofing Upgrade
verbatim_excerpt: Manatee County Capital Improvement Plan (Project #PJTP27011): District 4 12A Master Lift Station Upgrade allocated $2,361,000 in enterprise utility funds for replacement of aging submersible solids-handling pumps, Variable Frequency Drives (VFDs), Motor Control Centers (MCCs), wet-well ultrasonic level transducers, and floodproofed elevated SCADA control cabinets to mitigate Sanitary Sewer Overflows (SSOs).

project_title: Bonnie Wenk Sanitary Sewer Lift Station & SCADA Integration
verbatim_excerpt: City of McKinney Legistar Council Agenda Amendment (Project #PK2740 — Bonnie Wenk Sanitary Sewer Lift Station Project): Appropriates $200,000 from the Park Construction Fund balance into the Capital Improvements Program for duplex submersible lift station pumps, stainless steel guide rails, NEMA 4X control panel, and full citywide SCADA telemetry system integration.

project_title: Lift Station Generator, Control Cabinet & Chopper Pump Replacement
verbatim_excerpt: City of Plant City Capital Improvement Plan (Project UM019 — Lift Station Generator and Pump Replacement): Annualized station rehabilitation tranche of $485,000 within the broader $6,345,000 Water and Sewer Capital Outlay framework to replace lift station pumps past their 7-to-15 year useful life with non-clog chopper pumps combating flushable wipes, alongside emergency standby diesel generators and stainless control cabinet retrofits.

project_title: Pumping Station 17 Firm Capacity Pumps & PS2 VFD Replacements
verbatim_excerpt: Madison Metropolitan Sewerage District 2026 Capital Improvements Budget: Combined pumping station electromechanical package totaling $1,617,000 comprising Pumping Station 17 Firm Capacity Improvements ($1,527,000) and Pumping Station 2 Variable Frequency Drive (VFD) Replacements ($90,000) to replace obsolete dry-pit wastewater pumps, harmonic-mitigating 18-pulse VFDs, and magnetic flowmeters.

project_title: Pumping Station Mechanical Bar Screens & Washer-Compactor Replacement
verbatim_excerpt: Madison Metropolitan Sewerage District 2026 Capital Improvements Budget: Pumping Station Bar Screens Replacement estimated expenditure of $2,000,000 to replace corroded influent mechanical bar screens past useful life with multi-rake perforated/bar screening units, screenings washer-compactors, differential level PLC controls, and H2S-resistant enclosures.

agency: Department of Water Management — Wastewater Engineering
project_title: Parkwood Area Sanitary Sewer Lift Station Rehabilitation
verbatim_excerpt: City of Durham FY 2026 Capital Improvement Program (Water Management): Parkwood Area Lift Station authorized CIP budget of $2,700,000 for complete wet-well rehabilitation, triplex submersible wastewater pumps, automatic transfer switch (ATS), odor-control biofilter media unit, and cellular/radio SCADA RTU panel upgrade.

project_title: Neuse River Resource Recovery Facility UV Disinfection & Solids Renewal
verbatim_excerpt: City of Raleigh Adopted FY 2026 Budget & 5-Year CIP (Raleigh Water Asset Management Highlights): UV / Solids Handling renewal at Neuse River Resource Recovery Facility funded at $300,000 in FY 2026 for Basis-of-Design engineering and preliminary UV channel equipment specification, scaling across the 5-year CIP program horizon to $7,100,000 total construction and OEM UV disinfection bank procurement.

project_title: Residential Ultrasonic Smart Water Meter & AMI Endpoint Replacement
verbatim_excerpt: City of Naperville 2026 Capital Improvement Program & Legistar Account WU020 (Water Meter Replacement): Multi-year residential meter replacement tranche budgeted at $1,570,330 to replace aging mechanical positive-displacement meters past accuracy life with solid-state ultrasonic residential water meters, dual-port AMI smart radio endpoints, and pit-lid antennas.

project_title: Water Resource Recovery Facility Primary Clarifier Mechanism Overhaul
verbatim_excerpt: City of Boulder Utilities CIP (FY 2026-2031 OpenGov Portal): WRRF Clarifier Rehabilitation Project allocated $2,080,000 in Wastewater Utility Enterprise funds to overhaul aging primary clarifiers, replacing worn-out center-column drive mechanisms, 316L stainless steel sludge collector arms, scum skimmers, torque-overload PLC monitors, and effluent Launder covers.

project_title: Storm Water Quality Retrofits & Automated Flood Control Gate Telemetry
verbatim_excerpt: City of Bellevue 2025-2030 Storm and Surface Water Utility CIP: Storm Water Quality Retrofits funded at $1,296,000 (alongside companion Flood Control Program infrastructure) for hydrodynamic stormwater trash/sediment separators, high-rate media filtration vaults, automated actuated weir gates, and remote ultrasonic water-level telemetry sensors.

project_title: Influent/Bypass Pump Station & WWTP Electrical/Irrigation Pump Upgrades
verbatim_excerpt: Groveland Community Services District FY 2025/26 Wastewater Fund CIP Schedule: Active FY 2025/26 capital appropriations total $522,675 combining Influent and Bypass Pump Station Improvements ($186,300) and WWTP Electrical Evaluation & Irrigation Pump Station Construction ($336,375), whereas Complete SCADA System Upgrades shows $0 in FY 2025/26 (deferred to $110,872 in FY 2027/28 alongside $594,550 PLC/Radio replacement).

agency: Park & Recreation Department — Park Maintenance & Forestry
project_title: High-Use Playground Equipment, ADA Unitary Surfacing & Splash Pad Rehab
verbatim_excerpt: City of Wichita Adopted FY 2026 Capital Improvement Program (Parks & Recreation): Combined FY 2026 park amenity renewal of $530,000 comprising Playground Rehabilitation & Development ($450,000) to replace 18-year-old play structures with inclusive modular play towers and ASTM F1292 poured-in-place (PIP) rubber safety surfacing, plus Splash Pad Maintenance ($80,000) for aquatic solenoid manifold controllers and UV/chlorine recirculation skids.

agency: Parks and Recreation Department — Aquatics & Parks
project_title: Splash Park Recirculation System Reuse Phase 1 & Blue Earth Water Feature Rehab
verbatim_excerpt: City of Manhattan FY 2026 Capital Improvement Program (Parks & Aquatics): Allocates $325,000 across Splash Park Recirculation / Stingray Reuse Phase 1 (Project #CP466P at $200,000) and Blue Earth Water Feature Leaper Renovation (Project #CP411P at $125,000) for zero-depth splash pad recirculation filtration tanks, ORP/pH chemical controllers, low-voltage capacitive touch bollards, and stainless steel spray nozzles.

project_title: Agua Linda Park Splash Pad, Shade Structure & Playground Design/Spec
verbatim_excerpt: City of Scottsdale Adopted FY 2025/26 Capital Improvement Plan (Project TEMP3275 — Agua Linda Park Improvement Design): Appropriates $413,400 from the Park Improvements Fund for Basis-of-Design specification of inclusive playground equipment, integral tensioned fabric shade canopies, poured-in-place UV-stable safety surfacing, and neighborhood splash pad hydraulic controls ahead of construction bidding.

agency: Dept. of Neighborhood & Community Services / FCPS Facilities
project_title: Countywide Athletic Fields LED Sports Lighting Modernization
verbatim_excerpt: Fairfax County FY 2026-2030 Adopted Capital Improvement Program (Athletic Fields — FCPS Lighting Upgrades): Allocates $250,000 in FY 2026 General Fund capital ($1,250,000 five-year program total) to replace legacy 1500W metal halide fixtures past useful life with glare-shielded IES RP-6 compliant LED sports luminaires, galvanized cross-arms, and wireless cellular scheduling cabinets.

agency: Saint Paul Parks and Recreation — Design & Construction
project_title: Horton Park Exterior LED Pole Fixture & Electrical Service Replacement
verbatim_excerpt: City of Saint Paul 2026 Capital Improvement Budget (CIB Cost Review — Horton Park Lighting): Approved cost estimate of $89,650 for removal of 9 obsolete high-pressure sodium park luminaires, installation of dark-sky Type III cutoff LED pole fixtures on existing concrete footings, underground electrical service tie-in, and vandal-resistant photocell controls.

project_title: SWDE Arlington East WRF Disinfection Conversion to High-Level UV
verbatim_excerpt: JEA Capital Projects Committee & FY 2025-2027 CIP (SWDE Arlington East Water Reclamation Facility Disinfection Conversion to High Level UV): Approved Guaranteed Maximum Price (GMP) amendment of $26,457,694 within the $102,221,000 program budget for high-level closed/open-channel UV disinfection reactors, medium-voltage switchgear, slide gates, and auxiliary online analyzer instrumentation.
